h1: Land Rover Oil Leak & Gasket Repair

blocks.html: Oil leaks on Land Rover engines occur when gaskets or seals degrade over time. Our repair service targets the specific sealing failure without a full engine rebuild. We identify the source, replace the failed component, and test thoroughly to ensure the leak is permanently resolved.
We work on all common leak points: valve cover gaskets, sump gaskets, front and rear crankshaft seals, camshaft seals, timing cover gaskets, oil cooler gaskets, and turbocharger oil lines.

paras: **Get a fixed-price quote after inspection.** Every Land Rover is different; we diagnose the exact leak and provide a transparent quote before any work begins.

blocks.html: Oil leaks affect all Land Rover models. We repair gaskets and seals across the entire range.

steps.title: Diagnosis & Identification
steps.body: We clean the engine bay, apply UV dye (if needed), and run the engine to pinpoint the exact leak source.

steps.title: Access & Preparation
steps.body: We remove components blocking access – timing covers, transmission, or ancillaries – to reach the failed seal or gasket.

steps.title: Gasket / Seal Replacement
steps.body: Old gasket/seal removed, surfaces cleaned, new genuine or equivalent part fitted and torqued to specification.

steps.title: Testing & Quality Check
steps.body: Engine run to temperature, oil pressure checked, all repaired areas inspected for leaks, and road test performed.

items.q: What causes oil leaks on Land Rover engines?
items.a: Over time, gaskets and seals can degrade due to heat, pressure, and age. Common causes include valve cover gasket failure, sump gasket leakage, and crankshaft seal wear. We diagnose the exact cause during our inspection.

items.q: How long does a gasket repair take?
items.a: It depends on the location of the leak. Valve cover gaskets can be replaced in a few hours; rear main seals require transmission removal and may take a full day. We give a time estimate when we quote.

items.q: Will an oil leak repair fix all my problems?
items.a: If the leak is the only issue, then yes. However, if the oil leak has caused low oil pressure or contaminated the engine, additional work may be needed. We assess the overall engine condition during inspection.

items.q: Do you use genuine Land Rover gaskets?
items.a: We use genuine Land Rover parts or OE-equivalent parts with the same specification. For critical seals, we always recommend genuine components to ensure proper fit and longevity.

items.q: Is it worth repairing a small oil leak?
items.a: Yes. A small weep can quickly become a major leak, leading to low oil levels and potential engine damage. Repairing early is often more cost-effective than waiting for a larger failure.
